reproducibleNote: 2026-09-07: rebuilt for native-adapter ABI v2 (set_control gained a controller_index parameter; lucent_native_capabilities gained max_controllers). The one changed translation unit (engines/patches/aps3e-lucent-adapter.cpp) was recompiled directly with the exact clang++ invocation captured from the pinned tree's own compile_commands.json, then the shared library was relinked by running the exact link command `ninja -t commands` reported for it, both applied by hand rather than through a full `ninja` invocation of the target, because the tree's ninja-internal incremental state (.ninja_log/.ninja_deps) had just been invalidated (see below) and a plain `ninja <target>` would otherwise have forced a many-hour, from-scratch rebuild of the entire ~4,533-action graph (all of LLVM 19.1.7, FFmpeg, wolfSSL, etc.), not an incremental one. Every other .o/.a input to the link was the untouched output of the prior successful build; none were recompiled. Before editing, `git status` showed the working tree already matched HEAD for this source file with no local modifications. Real cause of the invalidation: an initial rebuild attempt used the ninja on this machine's PATH (1.13.2) instead of the pinned 1.10.2 (toolchain.ninjaVersion, bundled at $ANDROID_SDK/cmake/3.22.1/bin/ninja); ninja 1.13.2 printed 'build log version is too old; starting over' and rewrote .ninja_log/.ninja_deps in a newer, incompatible format, after which even the correct 1.10.2 binary treated the whole graph as stale. That attempt was killed as soon as it was noticed (it had only reached small early objects — curl/TableGen/LLVM leaf files) before it touched anything belonging to this adapter's own .o or the final .so, so the direct hand-compile-and-relink recovery above stayed valid; the corrupted ninja-internal state files were not restored and a future `ninja <target>` in this tree will still force that same full rebuild until it is reconfigured or its .ninja_log/.ninja_deps are regenerated by letting one complete. New artifact verified: correct ELF64 AArch64 shared object, same NEEDED list and 16 KiB (0x4000) PT_LOAD alignment as before, both lucent_native_adapter_entry and lucent_native_adapter_set_java_vm present in .dynsym after llvm-strip --strip-unneeded, size within 32 bytes of the prior unstripped build. Not independently re-verified on device. Previous: One source build and one incremental final relink were completed. No independent clean build has reproduced the exact binary, so this lock makes no reproducibility claim. The complete vendored dependency tree is source-pinned by the upstream commit, but its per-component license and notice inventory is not yet complete; the Phase 3 registry therefore keeps license and dependency gates false and shipped=false.

patches.note: Implements the in-window Vulkan adapter, DS3 control mapping, fail-closed user-firmware installation with a concrete version sentinel, lifecycle, persistent saves, RPCS3-native Quick Resume serialization, and a versioned JavaVM handoff that avoids upstream Activity-class registration. 2026-09-07: adopted native-adapter ABI v2's set_control(engine, controller_index, control, value) signature and describe()'s new max_controllers field. describe() honestly reports max_controllers = 1, not CELL_PAD_MAX_PORT_NUM's architectural 7: reading aps3e_rp3_impl.cpp (init_config(), AndroidVirtualPadHandler::bindPadToDevice()/Key(), pad_thread::Init()) confirmed that every player configured for the 'Keyboard' device shares ONE AndroidVirtualPadHandler instance and its single fixed 26-entry APS3E_VKC/mouse_list virtual-key space (codes 0-25), and that player 0's own default cfg_pad binds all 25 non-'none' codes one-to-one already, leaving no disjoint code range for a second player's independently-routable input without either widening that vendored enum/map or reaching into the handler's private per-instance m_pads_internal button list -- both changes outside this adapter translation unit and out of scope for this pass. set_control() now takes controller_index and, per the ABI's own documented contract for a max_controllers==1 adapter, treats any index other than 0 as a fail-closed no-op rather than aliasing it onto the primary player's state. No other logic in this file was touched.
